filament.name: Amolen Glow in the Dark PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini easily runs Amolen Glow PLA up to a safe maximum speed of 167 mm/s at 14 mm³/s volumetric flow, but you must replace the stock stainless steel hotend with a hardened steel assembly to prevent severe abrasive wear. Once upgraded, the direct drive system delivers dependable flow and reliable adhesion on the standard textured PEI plate.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate cleaned thoroughly with isopropyl alcohol (no adhesive required)
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at standard Bambu travel rates.
Increase Wall Loops to 3 or 4 to build thicker outer boundaries, enhancing phosphorescent light-storage and glow intensity.
Enable 'Wipe while Retracting' with a 2 mm wipe distance to control stringing caused by heavy phosphorescent particulate loading.
Set Outer Wall Speed to 100 mm/s and Inner Wall Speed to 160 mm/s to ensure optical surface uniformity without exceeding the flow limit.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid nozzle bore enlargement and inconsistent extrusion lines
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The abrasive strontium aluminate glow particles rapidly eroded the stock stainless steel nozzle tip.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an official Bambu Lab 0.4mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly before printing abrasive composite filaments.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and rough, fuzzy surface artifacts
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the PLA base polymer combined with heat-trapping phosphorescent additives.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 45°C for 6 hours before printing, and keep retraction speed at 30 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Intermittent hotend clogging during high-speed infill
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Attempting to exceed the 14 mm³/s volumetric limit, causing particulate clumping and backpressure in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set print temperature to 215°C and ensure OrcaSlicer max volumetric speed is clamped strictly to 14 mm³/s.

faq.question: Can I print Amolen Glow PLA on the stock A1 Mini out of the box?
faq.answer: No, the stock hotend has a stainless steel nozzle that will rapidly degrade from the abrasive phosphorescent particles, causing flow defects within a few hundred grams. You must first install the Bambu Lab hardened steel hotend.

faq.question: Does Amolen Glow PLA work with the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, it fits and feeds through the AMS Lite, but the abrasive filler will accelerate wear on the plastic funnel guides and PTFE tubing over prolonged use.

faq.question: How do I make the printed parts glow brighter?
faq.answer: Increase the number of wall loops to at least 4 and infill to 25% or higher, as more physical mass of strontium aluminate compound stores and radiates more light.

faq.question: Do I need an enclosure to print this filament on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No, Amolen Glow PLA is a modified PLA base that prints ideally in an open-air environment with standard 60°C bed temperatures and active part cooling.
